note: Both arms read one tree at one path -- the filesystem server reads the image's own /data in the run's container, and the mirage /data mount is a copy of it taken out of the same image -- so this compares two clients over one tree rather than two copies of it. The MCP server returns a file's bytes with a header line; the shell returns the bytes.

cases.name: list_directory
cases.why: both arms see the same tree -- the eight CSVs and the repos/ directory upstream's image also puts under /data -- which is the whole of the search this task is

cases.name: read_header
cases.why: the same file yields the same column names, so the two arms agree on which column holds the score

cases.name: row_count
cases.why: the same file has the same length, so a mean taken over it has the same denominator
